== /room/create REQUEST ADDITIONS (FEAT-002 sends these) ==
Body: presenceMonitoring: Bool, candidateRegionEU: Bool, candidateUnder18: Bool. Strict === true; anything else is false.
Arming writes SIX fields to the room hash and ONLY when armed:
  presenceMonitoringArmed='true', presenceRegionEU, presenceUnder18, presenceMultipleFacesEnabled (all 'true'/'false' strings),
  presenceDetectorVersion='presence-1.0.0', presenceThresholds=<JSON string>
DEVIATION (deliberate): the arming fields go in a SECOND conditional pipeline.hset() placed immediately after the existing one, not inside it. The existing hset call is therefore byte-for-byte unchanged, which is what makes the flag-off room hash provably identical to a pre-feature room (verified: 36 fields, zero presence keys).

== /room/join RESPONSE BLOCK (FEAT-002 parses these EXACT keys) ==
Present ONLY when roomData.presenceMonitoringArmed === 'true', otherwise the response has no key starting with "presence":
  presenceMonitoringArmed: true            (Bool)
  presenceRetentionDays: 90                (Int)
  presenceRegionEU: false                  (Bool)
  presenceUnder18: false                   (Bool)
  presenceMultipleFacesEnabled: false      (Bool)
  presenceDetectorVersion: "presence-1.0.0" (String)
  presenceThresholds: "{...}"              (STRING — the raw JSON text from the room hash, NOT an object. Parse it client-side.)
  presenceRightsContact: "privacy@kiomeet.invalid" (String)
NOTE for FEAT-002: there is no presenceConsentState / presenceMonitoringGranted on the join response. Consent state is the client's own record plus the POST /presence/consent response.
NOTE: the join block is gated on the ROOM HASH exactly as the plan specifies, not on the master flag. A room armed while the flag was on therefore keeps emitting this block until the room's 24 h Redis TTL expires, even after the flag is turned off — but the whole /presence surface returns 404 PRESENCE_DISABLED in that state, so consent cannot be granted and not one row can be written (asserted in presenceGate.test.js Group A).

== ENDPOINTS (mounted app.use('/presence', ...) after the app-level auth.authenticateToken) ==
Router-level first middleware: 404 {error:'Not found', code:'PRESENCE_DISABLED'} whenever isFeatureEnabled() is false.

1) POST /presence/consent            — header `Leave-Token: <token>`; body {roomCode, identity, decision:'grant'|'decline'}
   Rate limit presence-consent 10/600s. 200 -> {monitoringEnabled, consentState, consentVersion, retentionDays, rightsContact}
   consentState is 'granted'|'declined'. Upsert on (room_code, participant_identity); re-submitting is safe.
2) POST /presence/events             — header `Leave-Token: <token>`; body {roomCode, identity, events:[...]}
   Rate limit presence-events 30/60s. 200 -> {accepted:Int, gapRecorded:Bool}
3) GET  /presence/timeline/:code/:identity?callerIdentity=<moderatorIdentity>
   header `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Rate limit presence-timeline 60/60s.
4) POST /presence/timeline/:code/:identity/note
   header `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`; body {callerIdentity, eventId:Int, note:String}
   Rate limit presence-note 30/600s. 201 -> {noteId, createdAt, author}
5) GET  /presence/export/:code/:identity?format=json|csv&callerIdentity=<moderatorIdentity>
   header `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Rate limit presence-export 10/600s. format defaults to json.
callerIdentity is read from the query string on GET and from the body (query accepted as a fallback) on POST.
Candidate paths compare the Leave-Token with constantTimeEqual against redis.get(roomLeaveTokenKey(code, identity)) — a valid token for one identity does not authorise another. Moderator paths run auth.requireAuth THEN validateModerator(code, callerIdentity, req.user.userId).

== INGEST PAYLOAD SHAPE (FEAT-003 produces exactly this) ==
POST /presence/events
Headers: Content-Type: application/json, Leave-Token: <the leaveToken from /room/join>
{ "roomCode": "ABCDEF", "identity": "<participant identity>",
  "events": [ { "eventType": "face_absent",
                "startedAt": "2026-10-31T10:00:00.000Z",
                "endedAt":   "2026-10-31T10:00:12.000Z",
                "durationMs": 12000,
                "detectorVersion": "presence-1.0.0" } ] }
RULES FEAT-003 MUST HONOUR:
 * startedAt/endedAt are ISO-8601 STRINGS. A number is refused with 400 PRESENCE_PAYLOAD_INVALID (an epoch number is ambiguous between seconds and milliseconds and the server will not guess). Use ISO8601DateFormatter with fractional seconds; any valid ISO offset is accepted and normalised to UTC.
 * endedAt is optional (defaults to startedAt, giving durationMs 0 for the instantaneous camera transitions); durationMs is optional (derived from the interval) but must be a non-negative Int when present; endedAt must not precede startedAt.
 * Only the five keys above may appear per event, and only roomCode/identity/events at the top level. Anything else is a 400 — thresholds in particular are refused because the server stamps them.
 * An EMPTY events array is VALID and is the heartbeat. FEAT-003's reporter MUST POST on its 15 s cadence even when the buffer is empty: silence longer than PRESENCE_GAP_SECONDS (60) makes the SERVER record a monitoring_gap, and a clean session that simply never posts would be filled with gaps.
 * Batch limit 100 per request (101 -> 413). express.json() has no limit option so the 100 KB Express default body cap also applies.
 * multiple_faces is refused with 409 PRESENCE_EVENT_TYPE_DISABLED unless the room's presenceMultipleFacesEnabled is true. Per the plan the engine must not construct the event at all when the flag is off.
 * On 403 or 409 the reporter should stop reporting and report monitoring-off upward (plan item 19b).

== TIMELINE / EXPORT-JSON RESPONSE (FEAT-004 renders this) ==
{ monitoringEnabled: Bool, consentState: String, consentVersion: String|null,
  policyRegionEU: Bool, policyUnder18: Bool,
  detectorVersion: String, thresholds: Object, multipleFacesEnabled: Bool,
  sessionStartedAt: ISO, sessionEndedAt: ISO|null, sessionDurationMs: Int,
  summary: [ {eventType, count, totalDurationMs, liveSurfaceable} ],
  events:  [ {id, eventType, startedAt, endedAt|null, durationMs, offsetMs, detectorVersion,
              thresholds, source:'client'|'server', liveSurfaceable,
              notes:[{author, createdAt, text}] } ] }
DEVIATION: summary is an ARRAY, per plan section C's exact shape. Plan item 11's phrase "summary.byType" was not implemented — section C wins; presenceGate.test.js builds its own Map from the array.
A summary row has exactly those four keys and nothing else — asserted in presenceGate.test.js. There is no total, weighting, normalisation, percentage, rating, risk level or cross-candidate/cross-session comparison anywhere in the payload, and the code comment on the summary builder says so.
An OPEN gap (session live, silent longer than gapSeconds) is computed on the fly with id:null and endedAt:null and folded into summary; it is NOT persisted. The event list is capped at 2000 rows (LIMIT) while summary comes from a SQL GROUP BY, so the counts stay complete even in the implausible case of truncation.
offsetMs is the event's offset from sessionStartedAt — what jump-to-timestamp consumes.
liveSurfaceable is true only for multiple_faces and face_absent. image_quality_insufficient is deliberately FALSE: a data-quality fact about the video is never surfaced live as if it were candidate behaviour.

== CSV EXPORT ==
Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="presence-<code>-<identity>.csv"  (both parts through fileValidation.sanitizeFilename)
Header row, verbatim: event_type,started_at,ended_at,duration_ms,offset_ms,detector_version,source,thresholds_json
One row per event, CRLF line endings, every field wrapped in double quotes with internal quotes doubled, and any value beginning = + - or @ prefixed with an apostrophe (OWASP formula-injection guard).

== ERROR CODES (exact strings, as implemented) ==
INSUFFICIENT_TIER              403  reused existing string; response also carries currentTier and requiredTier:'hiring'
PRESENCE_DISABLED              404  master flag off (router's first middleware)
PRESENCE_MONITORING_NOT_ARMED  409  room exists but was never armed
PRESENCE_CONSENT_REQUIRED      409  ingest while consent is not 'granted' or monitoring is off
PRESENCE_EVENT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED 400 type not in CLIENT_EVENT_TYPES (covers monitoring_gap, head_off_axis and anything unknown)
PRESENCE_EVENT_TYPE_DISABLED   409  multiple_faces while the room gate is off
PRESENCE_FORBIDDEN_FIELD       400  a FORBIDDEN_KEYS key is present; response carries `field`
PRESENCE_UNKNOWN_FIELD         400  a key outside the allowlist; response carries `field`
PRESENCE_PAYLOAD_INVALID       400  shape/type/ordering violation; `field` when known
PRESENCE_BATCH_TOO_LARGE       413  more than 100 events
PRESENCE_SESSION_NOT_FOUND     404  no room hash, no session row for (code, identity), or a note aimed at an event outside the session
PRESENCE_UNAUTHORIZED          403  missing or mismatched Leave-Token
PRESENCE_FORBIDDEN             403  validateModerator rejected the caller
PRESENCE_NOTE_REASON_REQUIRED  400  note under 10 characters after trimming
ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE         500  crypto.isEncryptionAvailable() false on the note path; fails closed, writes nothing
PRESENCE_UNAVAILABLE           503  Redis or DB unreachable (including a Redis error inside the rate limiter)
RATE_LIMITED                   429  NEW string, always with a Retry-After header
auth.requireAuth's 401 carries NO code field (unchanged house behaviour) and these hand-written 4xx bodies carry no requestId (only the global error handler produces one).
RATE LIMITER DIVERGENCE, deliberate and commented in code: a Redis error returns 503 PRESENCE_UNAVAILABLE instead of failing open, because every one of these handlers needs Redis anyway for the room data and the leave token, and an unmetered flood of behavioural-record writes is the worse failure.

== AUDIT EVENTS (all through the injected auth.auditLog, never awaited, never carrying note text, email, thresholds-as-free-text or any forbidden key) ==
presence_consent_granted / presence_consent_declined   metadata {roomCode, identity, consentState}
presence_monitoring_enabled / presence_monitoring_disabled  metadata {roomCode, identity, policyRegionEU, policyUnder18}
presence_timeline_read                                 metadata {roomCode, identity, eventCount}
presence_note_added                                    metadata {roomCode, identity, eventId, noteLength}
presence_export                                        metadata {roomCode, identity, format, eventCount}
presence_events_purged (sweeper)                       metadata {eventRows, sessionRows, retentionDays}, userId null
userId is null for a guest candidate; the ephemeral identity lives in metadata. Observed in the live DB after the test runs: all seven router-written types present. audit_events rows cannot be deleted (migration 011 trigger) — the tests assert presence only and never attempt cleanup.

== MIGRATION 023 ==
Three tables, IF NOT EXISTS throughout, every FK naming its ON DELETE policy with the reason in a comment: meeting_id CASCADE, host_user_id SET NULL, candidate_user_id SET NULL, session_id CASCADE, event_id CASCADE, author_user_id SET NULL. event_type CHECK lists exactly the six types and DOES NOT contain head_off_axis. thresholds JSONB NOT NULL, detector_version TEXT NOT NULL and purge_after TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL on both sessions and events. note_text_enc TEXT NOT NULL + note_key_version SMALLINT NOT NULL. No email, no display name on the session row. Indexes: idx_ips_room_identity (UNIQUE), idx_ips_purge_due, idx_ips_stale (partial), idx_ipe_session_time, idx_ipe_purge_due, idx_ipe_session_type, idx_ipn_event. updated_at trigger on sessions only (DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS first so a re-run is clean).

== KNOWN MATCHING LIMIT, recorded on purpose ==
FORBIDDEN_KEYS is matched by EXACT comparison of normalised keys, which is the rule the plan states.
